EnLink Midstream, LLC's FY2023 Form 10-K (SEC CIK 1592000), Exhibit 21.1 (subsidiaries of the registrant), lists 'Sabine Pipe Line LLC' (Delaware) directly under the Sabine Pass Plant Facility Joint Venture grouping alongside 'Sabine Ethane, LLC' and 'Sabine Hub Services LLC' -- confirming Sabine Pipe Line LLC as an EnLink subsidiary as of that filing (matches the row's route, Erath LA to Port Arthur TX, and the 'Sabine' naming). CRITICAL MERGER-CHURN NOTE, applies to this row only within this brief (not shared with any other row here): ONEOK, Inc. completed its acquisition of 100% of EnLink Midstream, LLC on January 31, 2025 (previously ONEOK held only a ~40-44% economic interest via general-partner and limited-partner stakes). ONEOK's own Form 8-K (SEC CIK 1039684, filed 2025-01-31) describes the merger structure: a wholly-owned ONEOK merger subsidiary merged with and into EnLink Midstream, LLC, with EnLink surviving as, ultimately, a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of ONEOK. Because this is a DIFFERENT SEC registrant/CIK (1039684 ONEOK vs. 1592000 EnLink) reporting the same event, this counts as two independent origins under this project's sourcing rule, so tier=high/independent=true. Staged value is 'EnLink Midstream' (matching the existing sheet Owner naming convention, not the more specific subsidiary 'Sabine Pipe Line LLC') because EnLink Midstream is now itself a wholly-owned ONEOK subsidiary rather than an independent public company -- ONEOK is the ultimate parent as of Jan 2025, but EnLink Midstream retains its own name and continues to operate/report the legacy EnLink asset base (including Sabine) as a distinct corporate entity, per ONEOK's 8-K. A human should decide whether to record 'EnLink Midstream' (operating-entity level, matches existing Owner) or escalate to 'ONEOK' (ultimate-parent level, post-Jan-2025) as the Operator of record -- this is a genuine post-acquisition naming-convention call, not a sourcing gap.
